olivia (docs): Quick catch from an onboarding report: our Docker quickstart shows copying a local .env into the image and exposes port 8080, but the sample server actually listens on 3000. New users are building images that leak env files into published images and then wonder why the container crashes.

olivia (docs): Problematic Dockerfile snippet we found in quickstarts/docker/README.md: ```Dockerfile
# BAD - copies .env into image and publishes wrong port
FROM node:18
WORKDIR /app
COPY . /app
RUN npm ci --only=production
EXPOSE 8080
CMD ["node", "server.js"]
```

ben (devex): Yikes. That not only encourages committing/packaging secrets but also mismatched port mapping is causing failed healthchecks on our examples. I had a user run `docker run -p 8080:8080 image` and then open http://localhost:8080 and see nothing.

satish (sdk): I'll prep a PR. Proposed replacement: ```Dockerfile
# GOOD - don't copy .env, multi-stage, explicit build args, correct port + healthcheck
FROM node:18 AS builder
WORKDIR /app
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci
COPY src ./src
RUN npm run build

FROM node:18-slim
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=builder /app/dist ./dist
# use build-arg or runtime env, never copy .env into image
ARG REDWOOD_API_KEY
ENV REDWOOD_API_KEY=$REDWOOD_API_KEY
EXPOSE 3000
HEALTHCHECK --interval=10s --timeout=3s CMD curl -f http://localhost:3000/health || exit 1
CMD ["node", "dist/server.js"]
```

satish (sdk): In the README I'll show the recommended run: `docker run -e REDWOOD_API_KEY=$REDWOOD_API_KEY -p 3000:3000 mysample` and a note about using docker secrets or a managed secret store for production. Also adding a note to add .env to .dockerignore (and .gitignore).

olivia (docs): Please also update the quickstart docs to call out the mismatch and add a short troubleshooting bullet: "If the server appears down, check that you're forwarding port 3000 and didn't copy a .env into the image."

ci-bot: docs-lint: failure -> quickstarts/docker/README.md line 22: detected pattern matching '\\.(env|secrets?)' being copied into image. Link: https://ci.internal/jobs/7781

ben (devex): Can we add a docs-validator rule to detect COPY . /app or COPY . . in Dockerfile code fences and flag when a .env exists in the repository? It would catch accidental copies.

satish (sdk): Good idea. I'll add two checks to docs-validator: 1) flag COPY . / when a .env or .env.* is present in the repo snapshot, 2) ensure exposed port in Dockerfile matches the sample server port in the quickstart (basic regex cross-check). Also adding a tiny CI job to fail docs on literal sk- token patterns in Dockerfiles.

olivia (docs): I'll open issue #1210 and include the user report and the proposed Dockerfile snippet. Once PR is ready, I'll update the onboarding checklist and add a short note to the changelog so folks who copied the old Dockerfile get notified.

ben (devex): Thanks everyone. Small change but avoids secrets leakage and a bunch of "my container doesn't respond" posts. :lock: :shipit:"
